Agents.title: Claude Code Packs
Agents.intro: The complete kit for working with Claude Code — memory, skills and commands in native format: <claudeMd></claudeMd> + <skillsDir></skillsDir> + <commandsDir></commandsDir>, following the <skillMd></skillMd> standard used by <skillsShLink></skillsShLink>. It also includes a kit of <subagentsLink></subagentsLink> (<agentsDir></agentsDir>). Self-contained: it doesn't depend on any other agent.
Agents.stacksAvailable: {count, plural, one {# stack available} other {# stacks available}}

Subagentes.metaDescription: The kit's subagents for Antigravity and Claude Code: what each one does, which ones write code and which are read-only.
Subagentes.intro: A subagent runs in its own context window, with its own allowed tools and its own model. The details of its work — the 40 files it read to find one — never come back to the main conversation: the result does. Each tool has its own format; the kit ships subagents for both.
Subagentes.whatIsBody: Either way it's a Markdown file with frontmatter: name, description (how the main agent decides when to delegate), allowed tools and model. What differs is the path, how it's invoked and the tool names — which is why the kit doesn't convert one into the other, it ships a native set per tool.
Subagentes.formatNote: Antigravity also accepts global subagents in ~/.gemini/config/agents/, isolation via Git worktree and up to 10 levels of nesting. The ones in the kit are workspace-scoped: they travel with the project.
Subagentes.downloadBody: Subagents are the same for any stack, so they come preselected in every preset. You can also build the ZIP by hand and pick only the ones you want.

SkillCatalog.title: Skill Catalog
SkillCatalog.intro: Every skill in one place so you can decide what to install in the project at hand: what each one is for, when to use it, the exact install command and how it's invoked. Prefer them grouped by type of work (SEO, Web, Backend...)? <byProjectLink></byProjectLink>.
SkillCatalog.origins: The ones marked <hub></hub> already ship here and can be downloaded together from <buildLink></buildLink>. The <external></external> ones are third-party: installed separately, with their own command.

SkillsByProject.title: Skills by project type
SkillsByProject.intro: Skills combined by the kind of work you're doing — the same skill can show up in more than one category. Prefer them all together in a single table? <catalogLink></catalogLink>.
SkillsByProject.noInstallFallback: Included directly in the /build ZIP — no separate install needed.
